subject: Proposal: Remote COLA grid and offer adjustments (US / EU / APAC)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Remote COLA grid and offer adjustments (US / EU / APAC)

Hi Laura / Maya —

Putting this on your radar and asking for HR / comp guidance. We have a few open senior ICs and a manager role where recruiting is pushing to localize offers for candidates in Germany and India. Historically we used the same band for remote US hires and adjusted EU/APAC with one-off notes, but hiring velocity + market movement means we should formalize a small COLA grid so hiring managers have clear guidance.

High-level proposal (attached spreadsheet: COLA_grid_v2.xlsx):
- US (remote): baseline band = market midpoint, no automatic COLA except metro allowances for SF/NYC 
- EU: +8–12% uplift depending on cost index (Germany/NL/SE on the higher end)
- APAC: +6–10% uplift; India-specific concession +4% for senior roles given budget constraints

Ask:
1) Can HR confirm these ranges are OK by band (IC3 / IC4 / Mgr)?
2) For offers > 12% uplift we’ll route to compensation committee — ok?
3) Maya: do we have headcount budget to absorb the midpoints for Q4 (see attached headcount_request_ENGQ4.pdf)?

I want to avoid ad-hoc negotiates and multiple rework cycles in Offer Team — a small table hiring managers can reference would help speed offers.

Thanks,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Product Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Remote COLA grid and offer adjustments (US / EU / APAC)

Thanks Marcus — good initiative. I attached an updated COLA_grid_v2.xlsx with band-specific suggested uplifts and a short rationale column (market index + competing offer heat). A few notes from comp: 

- The ranges look reasonable; we should anchor to band midpoints (IC3/IC4/Mgr) and avoid percentage stacking (e.g., metro allowance + COLA) unless the role is location-tied.
- For Germany/Netherlands/Sweden we recommend +10–12% at senior IC and +12% for manager candidates in high-cost metros.
- India: agree on conservative +4% for senior ICs; manager roles should be handled case-by-case because of local grade compression.

Approval workflow: any offer that results in a delta > 15% from the candidate's expected midpoint or > $25k comp delta requires compensation committee review. If you want, I can pre-authorize a "fast-track" up to 10% for heads of engineering if Maya confirms budget.

Action items I can take:
- Finalize the grid into an HR-approved reference table (we'll publish in Confluence).
- Add a short FAQ for recruiters about when to route to CC.

Marcus — please share the specific candidates/roles you want to close this week and I’ll pre-populate the recommended offer amounts.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: COLA_grid_v2.xlsx

Subject: Re: Proposal: Remote COLA grid and offer adjustments (US / EU / APAC)

Marcus / team — thanks for looping me in. Quick market note from the recruiter side:

- Germany: candidates are now asking for "local parity" to EU peers. If you quote only a 6–8% uplift you'll see counteroffers from EU-based companies. 
- India: top senior engineers are price elastic; a stronger equity package (Vested RSUs or higher target bonus) is often more cost-effective than salary uplift.
- APAC (SG/HK): expect a premium for cloud-native infra expertise — 8–12% typical.

Happy to share anonymized comps from three active processes if it's helpful. We can also push for faster closing if you ok a pre-approved 8% flexible uplift for senior ICs.

Cheers,
Jane
Talent Partner — Talentscape (external)
